leading_positions.synthesis: All six round-1 configurations are a single-part B042 (GLP-1) prize. Five members (Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) name Drucker, Holst and Mojsov with a citation centred on the physiology and active peptide form of GLP-1. El-Manira names Drucker, Holst and Knudsen with a citation that includes the development of long-acting GLP-1-based therapies. Shared: Drucker and Holst, a three-person single-part prize, and the view that maturity and clinical consequence are very high. Not shared: whether the third place goes to Mojsov (identification of the active peptide) or Knudsen (long-acting analogues), and whether the citation is framed as discovery or as discovery plus therapy development.

areas_of_agreement: All six members ranked B042 first in the opening and all six retain it as the sole part of their round-1 configuration.
Drucker and Holst appear in all six configurations.
Maturity of B042 is not seriously disputed: independent confirmation over decades, multiple approved agents and large randomised outcome trials in glycaemia, weight, cardiovascular and renal disease.

Every member names attribution at the three-person cap as the main weakness of B042, and every member states that priority details (Mojsov, Habener, Knudsen) are recalled rather than verified from the supplied files.
B033 (unfolded protein response; Mori and Walter) is the most frequent alternative, listed by all six members, and is described as a compact, well-attributed pair with weaker direct clinical payoff.
No member reports a conflict that affects the proposed B042 configurations.
scientific_disputes: Whether the prize should honour discovery of GLP-1 physiology and its active peptide (the five-member Mojsov configuration) or also the step from native peptide to durable long-acting drug (El-Manira's inclusion of Knudsen, who argues this is a scientific achievement in protein chemistry and pharmacology rather than routine optimisation).

Whether the second-ranked alternatives are comparable in readiness: B033 is favoured for basic-science clarity, B049 (CAR-T) as the strongest translational alternative but with limited efficacy beyond B-cell malignancies, and B045 (optogenetics) for its impact on circuit dissection, with members disagreeing on how much clinical consequence should weigh against foundational biology.
Open mechanistic and safety questions for the obesity indication (central mechanisms, long-term safety) were raised by Svenningsson; other members treat the evidence as sufficiently mature.
attribution_disputes: B042 third place: Mojsov (Linnarsson, Perlmann, Sandberg, Svenningsson, Wahren-Herlenius) versus Knudsen (El-Manira). El-Manira states he would accept swapping Mojsov in for Knudsen if the peptide-identification record proves firmer than he can verify; the other five state that excluding Knudsen leaves the prize open to the charge of ignoring drug development.

Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide is described as contested in public accounts by all members, and Habener is not among the credited names.

B049 (CAR-T): the credited names are June, Sadelain and Rosenberg, while Eshhar is absent; Sandberg proposes a two-person June and Sadelain version, and El-Manira notes that dropping a name does not resolve the Eshhar omission.

B045 (optogenetics): six credited names; El-Manira states that no three-person subset avoids serious exclusions and that the channelrhodopsin discoverers (Nagel, Hegemann) map differently from Deisseroth, Boyden and Miesenboeck.
B012 (deep brain stimulation): a single-laureate credit for Benabid omits basal ganglia and subthalamic circuit contributions such as DeLong, which was raised as a reason for caution.
maturity_disputes: No member argues that B042 should wait. Maturity disputes concern alternatives: B045 is described as not close to prize-ready because of attribution, B006 (TOR) was ranked second by Linnarsson but is described by El-Manira as having modest clinical consequence and unsettled credit among Hall, Schreiber and Sabatini, and B033 is seen as mature but with a weaker direct clinical payoff.
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Perlmann discloses documented co-authorship with Svenningsson and notes that B012 (deep brain stimulation for Parkinson's disease) is close to his own Parkinson's-related research; neither bears on his configuration.

Svenningsson discloses a Rockefeller postdoctoral period with Paul Greengard and about twenty co-authored works with Perlmann, and flags that B012 and B045 are in his clinical and research neighbourhood and would be flagged if they came to the front; none involves a person credited for B042, B033 or B049.
El-Manira discloses a 2009 co-authored paper with Perlmann and a 2019 review with Sten Grillner, and notes that optogenetics (B045) is close to his field as topical familiarity only.
Linnarsson and Sandberg disclose shared co-authors and joint publications with each other and with others who are not credited on a shortlisted ballot; no recusal is proposed by any member.
questions_for_round2: For B042, should the third laureate be Mojsov or Knudsen, and what specific evidence in the supplied record (not recollection) settles Mojsov's priority relative to Habener and others for the active peptide?

Should the B042 citation be framed around discovery of GLP-1 physiology and its active peptide form, or should it explicitly include the development of long-acting GLP-1-based therapies, and does that framing decide the third name?
Is a two-part prize combining B042 with B033 (or B049) worth the loss of a name from B042 under the three-person limit, and if so which names would be dropped from each part?
If B033 is held as the fallback or second part, does its weaker direct clinical payoff matter under the criteria, and does its compact Mori and Walter attribution outweigh that?
For B049, can any three-name or two-name configuration be defended given the absence of Eshhar from the credited list, or should the committee treat attribution as blocking this year?
summary.chair_observation: Round 1 shows strong convergence on B042 as a single-part prize and a narrow, specific disagreement on whether the third place and the citation emphasise discovery (Mojsov) or therapy development (Knudsen). The count is five configurations with Mojsov and one with Knudsen, all of which rely on recalled rather than verified priority details. Second-part alternatives are listed but no member has proposed a two-part configuration in round 1.
